$comment: Home-page demo: a real consultation, run on the live site (bigjospaints.vercel.app/colour-consultant) on 11 Oct 2026 with OpenAI GPT-5.5. The photo is a real lounge photographed by Sven Brandsma on Unsplash (src/assets/photos/living-room.jpg; credit in src/lib/photos.ts), sent at 1600 px as the consultant's own upload does. The brief is as sent. roomRead, title, why and tip are the AI's words, unedited; litres and prices are worked out from catalogue.json when the site is built, exactly as the consultant does. public/demo/walls.png marks the pink walls (white = wall) for the tinted preview: picked by colour (CIELAB hue, chroma, lightness) inside the back wall, with the window view, photo frames, hanging pot and cabinet cut out by hand.
brief: Our lounge is a dusty pink and we're ready for a change. Something calm but still warm, to go with the wood stove, the oak floor and our plants.
roomRead: Your lounge has good side light, warm oak flooring, a black wood stove with brick, lots of creamy trim and natural plant greens, so a warm calm neutral or soft sage will sit better than the current dusty pink.

options.title: Warm and easy
options.why: This sandy beige keeps the warmth of the oak floor and stove area, but feels calmer and more timeless than pink. It will also work well with the grey sofa and cream macramé.
options.tip: Keep the ceiling and trim in a soft white so the room stays bright.

options.title: Soft natural calm
options.why: This pale sage picks up the plants and softens the black stove without making the lounge feel cold. It is light enough for all walls in your 6 × 4 m room.
options.tip: Pair it with warm oak, woven textures and off-white curtains or blinds.

options.title: Quiet greige warmth
options.why: This classic greige is a safe, grown-up shift from dusty pink while still feeling warm beside the oak and brick. It will make the grey sofa look intentional rather than heavy.
options.tip: Add a few terracotta or rust cushions to echo the fire and keep the scheme cosy.
